# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_003_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 1, Chapter 3

**1** When she finished talking, she asked me, "Would you like me to read to you?" "Very much," I said. "Then listen carefully." She opened the book and began to read — wonderful, magnificent things, far beyond anything I could hold in my memory. The words were overwhelming, almost terrifying; no ordinary person could have endured hearing them. Only the final words stayed with me, because they were within human reach, and they were comforting: **2** "Look: the God of all power — who created the world through his great strength and wisdom, who clothed creation with beauty through his glorious design, who set the heavens in place and founded the earth on the waters through his mighty word, and through his wise and foreseeing care shaped his holy church and blessed it — this God is shaking the heavens, the mountains, the hills, the seas. Everything is being made level for his chosen people, so that he can fulfill the great and glorious promise he made to them — if they will keep the commandments he has given them in great faith and with great joy." **3** When the reading was done she stood up from the chair, and four young men came and carried the chair off toward the east. She reached out, touched my chest, and asked, "Did you enjoy what I read?" "The ending was beautiful," I told her, "but the beginning was harsh and frightening." She explained: "Those final words are for the righteous — the beginning was for the unbelievers and those who have fallen away." **4** While we were still talking, two men appeared and helped her up by the arms, and they all went off toward the east where the chair had gone. She left with a smile on her face, and as she went she called back to me: "Be strong, Hermas!"

---

*PNEUMA note: "Be strong" renders the Greek andrizo — literally "be manly/act like a man"; rendered idiomatically for modern readers.*
